proposition: Whether Ibn Turka was primarily an occult philosopher (a universalist lettrist) rather than a mystical philosopher, a Shiʿi esotericist or an orthodox Sunni Sufi is contested: Melvin-Koushki's thesis rests chiefly on lettrist works that are mostly still unedited, the rival readings on the Tamhid and the apologies.

mediation.note: MK's own interpretation, offered in support of his thesis that Ibn Turka was an occult philosopher.
